question.title: Coat Check Counter
question.content:
A cloakroom has hooks numbered from 1 to hooks. Implement the CoatCheck class:

  • CoatCheck(int hooks) Opens the cloakroom with every hook free.
  • int hang(String owner) Hangs the coat of owner on the lowest numbered free hook and returns that number, or returns -1 if no hook is free.
  • int collect(String owner) Frees the hook holding the coat of owner and returns its number, or returns -1 if owner has no coat here.
  • void clear() Takes every coat off, so that all hooks are free.

 

Example 1:

Input
["CoatCheck", "hang", "hang", "collect", "hang"]
[[2], ["ann"], ["bo"], ["ann"], ["cy"]]
Output
[null, 1, 2, 1, 1]

Explanation
CoatCheck coatCheck = new CoatCheck(2);
coatCheck.hang("ann");    // return 1
coatCheck.hang("bo");     // return 2
coatCheck.collect("ann"); // return 1, hook 1 is free again
coatCheck.hang("cy");     // return 1

Example 2:

Input
["CoatCheck", "hang", "hang", "clear", "collect", "hang"]
[[1], ["ann"], ["bo"], [], ["ann"], ["bo"]]
Output
[null, 1, -1, null, -1, 1]

Explanation
CoatCheck coatCheck = new CoatCheck(1);
coatCheck.hang("ann");    // return 1
coatCheck.hang("bo");     // return -1, the only hook is taken
coatCheck.clear();
coatCheck.collect("ann"); // return -1, the coat is gone
coatCheck.hang("bo");     // return 1

 

Constraints:

  • 1 <= hooks <= 1000
  • 1 <= owner.length <= 10
  • owner consists of lowercase English letters.
  • An owner never hangs a second coat while the first is still here.
  • At most 104 calls will be made to hang, collect, and clear.
